answer: Each applicant escrows a refundable bond and reserves one exclusive plot on a public terrain grid, a mesa cell the registry will not double-book in the epoch. They commit the hash of a physical one-use token they actually hold — about walnut size, uniquely serialized — and may reveal it only after a 12-hour delay; a reused or early preimage burns the bond. They post a short sonnet-length measurement note for peers to check. N identities cost N bonds, N exclusive cells, and N unreuseable tokens; a collision forfeits the stake, so attack cost scales linearly in locked capital plus scarce plots.
